requirements.title: The application shall add a new habit by name through the "Add habit" input and Add button, showing it immediately in the habit list

vision.paraphrase: Goal G1: a new habit appears in the list immediately after being added.

conops.paraphrase: Submitting the add form produces a full row — name, streak 0, checkbox, Archive action — at once.

requirements.title: The application shall submit the "Add habit" input when the user presses Enter, behaving identically to clicking Add

vision.paraphrase: Instant, low-friction interaction: Enter should feel the same as the button.

conops.paraphrase: The scenario explicitly allows pressing Enter as the add gesture.

requirements.title: The application shall persist a newly added habit so that it survives a page reload

vision.paraphrase: Goal G1's success criterion: the added habit survives a page reload.

conops.paraphrase: Reloading proves the habit stuck — the user's proof the app keeps its word.

requirements.title: The application shall reject an empty or whitespace-only habit name with an inline error that names the problem and the next user action

vision.paraphrase: Validation failures follow the error standard: name the problem and the next action, inline.

conops.paraphrase: The add input expects a typed name; submitting nothing must be refused, not silently ignored.

requirements.title: The application shall enforce a maximum habit-name length of 80 characters, accepting a name of exactly 80 characters and rejecting 81 or more

vision.paraphrase: Habit management is name-only with a bounded length so rows stay readable on one line.

conops.paraphrase: The add flow's boundary condition at the 80-character limit.

requirements.title: The application shall allow duplicate habit names, creating a second independent habit row

vision.paraphrase: Duplicates are deliberately allowed — the MVP adds no uniqueness machinery.

conops.paraphrase: Two same-named habits must track completions independently of each other.

requirements.title: The application shall archive a habit on demand, removing it from the Active view while preserving its completion history

vision.paraphrase: Archive is a core habit-management capability: out of the daily list, history kept.

conops.paraphrase: Clicking Archive on the row declutters the Active view without destroying anything.

requirements.title: The application shall restore an archived habit on demand, returning it to the Active view with its completion history intact

vision.paraphrase: Goal G4: archived habits are restorable.

conops.paraphrase: Restore puts a dropped habit back into rotation with zero data loss.
